summary: Guidance and safe backout for dynamic optimizer flags causing tail latency spikes
description: Issue summary: After enabling dynamic optimizer flags (auto-batching threshold + aggressive KV prefetch) for AcmeML's Dedicated pool, they reported a recurring tail latency increase affecting ~12% of requests. Impact: customer-facing APIs intermittently see 500–900 ms tail spikes and occasional streaming disconnects during peak hours. Environment: Dedicated cluster in prod.us-east, reserved capacity (p3d-equivalent), workload is mix of short chat requests (avg 150 tokens) and long completions (avg 800 tokens). Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer routing to send a burst of mixed-length requests (2000 qps for 3m) to pinned model redwood/rw-7b-q8_0. 2) Observed behavior under optimization flags: increased 95th/99th latency, occasional 5xx on streaming SSE connection. 3) Revert to static conservative config: latency returns to baseline. Observed vs Expected: Expected throughput improvement with same or slightly better p50/p90; instead p95/p99 regressed ~2x during bursts. Recent changes: patch enabling 'dynamic_batch_threshold=0.6' and 'kv_prefetch_aggressiveness=high' deployed 2026-03-11 at 02:10 UTC. Logs and traces: traces show long queue times on kernel selection and bursts of KV cache misses. Attachments: traces link, perf dashboards, sample request IDs. Request: Provide a safe backout checklist, immediate mitigation steps for customer, and recommendations for tuning flags to avoid recurrence.
comments: Support Engineer - Nina Patel - 2026-03-12: Initial triage completed. Observed correlation between deploy of dynamic flags and latency increase. Customer provided heap of traces and a Grafana snapshot. Customer impacted subset: ~3 of 8 routes critical to their product.

SRE - Marcus Lee - 2026-03-12: Noted increased variance in batch sizes and a higher rate of kv cache misses for long-context requests. Reproduced locally with synthetic workload. Hypothesis: aggressive prefetch + lower dynamic batch threshold causes fragmentation and forces more small batches on slow tail requests.

Support Engineer - Nina Patel - 2026-03-13: Customer requests immediate remediation while we investigate permanent fix. They've asked for a step-by-step safe backout they can run with minimal disruption.
Engineer - Diego Martinez - 2026-03-13: Drafted backout checklist below and asking SRE to validate edge cases (rolling back on Dedicated without node restart).
Customer - AcmeML-ops - 2026-03-13: We can schedule a maintenance window at 2026-03-14 01:00 UTC if needed. Need to avoid losing pinned model versions or interrupting long-running sessions.

SRE - Marcus Lee - 2026-03-14: Confirmed backout steps are safe for Dedicated: feature flags can be toggled at routing layer and optimizer config can be rolled via config-store with zero pod restarts when staged. Will assist during customer window.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC dynamic flags enabled; 2026-03-11 03:00 first latency alert; 2026-03-12 11:00 customer escalated. Hypotheses tested: (1) KV prefetch may evict useful cache items due to aggressive prefetching patterns -> increased remote loads. (2) Dynamic batching threshold set too low causing many small batches during mixed workloads -> overhead dominates. (3) Kernel selection contention when many small batches co-exist with a few large-context requests. What we ran: replayed production traffic into a staging Dedicated pool, toggled kv_prefetch_aggressiveness from high->medium->low and dynamic_batch_threshold from 0.6->0.85->1.0. Results: raising batch threshold to 0.95 eliminated p99 spikes at cost of 6% throughput reduction; lowering kv_prefetch to medium cut remote cache miss rate by 70% and tail latency improved. Metrics referenced: batch_size_distribution, kv_cache_miss_rate, kernel_wait_ms, serve_worker_cpu. Logs: sample trace IDs provided (trace-20260311-1a2b3c). Related runbook: confluence.redwood/inference/optimizer-flags-playbook. Edge cases: sessions using long live streams may observe rebuffering if we change kv prefetch mid-session — recommend graceful throttle for streams.
resolution: Immediate mitigation applied: During customer maintenance window (2026-03-14 01:00 UTC), we staged config change in config-store and ramped dynamic_batch_threshold to 0.95 and kv_prefetch_aggressiveness to medium for AcmeML's routing policy. Changes were staged behind feature flag and applied with canary to 10% traffic for 5 minutes then 100%. Observed: p95/p99 returned to baseline, throughput decreased 4% which is acceptable to customer. Workaround: If customer prefers maximum throughput, suggest scheduled off-peak enablement of aggressive flags with traffic shaping. Permanent recommendations: 1) Add a pre-deploy performance gate in the deployment pipeline that runs a short mixed-length replay and fails if p99 increases >20%. 2) Introduce an optimizer-profiles catalog (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with documented tradeoffs and defaults per workload mix. 3) Add automatic fallback: when kv_cache_miss_rate > 15% AND p99 increases >30% for more than 2 min, automatically restore conservative profile for the affected routing policy. Follow-ups: (a) engineering ticket to add the performance gate and automatic fallback (linked as INT-33145), (b) docs update to console UI to show active optimizer profile and one-click backout, (c) postmortem with customer scheduled. Owner: Diego Martinez. Time to resolution: 26 hours from first alert to full remediation.

public_notes_for_customer: Summary: We identified that a combination of lower dynamic batch threshold and high kv prefetch aggressiveness caused batch fragmentation and higher cache misses that led to tail latency spikes. Action taken: staged conservative optimizer profile (batch threshold 0.95, kv_prefetch medium), rolled out via canary, validated metrics returned to baseline. Next steps: schedule a tuning session to select the right profile for your traffic mix and add deployment safeguards. If you want aggressive flags again, we'll coordinate an off-peak experiment with detailed perf gating.
resolution_status: Mitigated (temporary config change); permanent changes TBD
